title: lichend leaves an unzeroized identity-seed copy in its long-lived main frame
description: Security review finding: lichend copies *seed.as_bytes() into a plain [u8;32] sealing_seed before constructing trust/slot/GatewayPersistence owners. The local remains in the async main state for the daemon lifetime and is never zeroized; GatewayPersistence also holds a plain array until new_persistent moves/copies it, including early-error paths. This defeats the Zeroizing fields added to the eventual owners and leaves an unnecessary private-key duplicate in stack/future memory. Carry the seed as Zeroizing<[u8;32]> end-to-end (including GatewayPersistence), minimize copies, and explicitly zeroize the caller's buffer immediately after all owners derive/move their protected material; exercise early returns.
